original_test_intent: Verify for every required E1.S bay that the correctly identified drive can enter the vendor-defined safe ready-to-remove state and that the mapped indicator simultaneously shows solid white with amber and green extinguished, without data loss or storage/platform errors.
original_method: Select the unique row; map chassis/backplane bay, controller, namespace and drive serial/model/firmware; baseline mounts, open users, multipath/RAID/LVM membership, health and preserved logs; insert using the approved service procedure; quiesce I/O and execute only the vendor-approved logical offline/detach or enclosure action needed to assert removal readiness; prove no active references remain; operator photographs the exact bay's simultaneous white-on/amber-off/green-off state; do not physically remove unless separately authorized; restore or leave the drive in the approved final state.
manual_activity: A qualified operator verifies the safe-service prerequisites, observes and photographs the exact three-color LED state and owns any separately approved physical removal or reinsertion.
required_inputs: Chassis/backplane and bay-slot-controller to drive serial/model/firmware/namespace map
Authoritative ready-to-remove trigger and state: OS offline, NVMe detach, enclosure locate/remove command, BMC action or other vendor sequence
White/amber/green LED position, simultaneous-state and stabilization specification
Hot-plug/ESD procedure, final drive state and recovery path
safety_requirements: Prove exact namespace/serial and exclude active OS, boot, mounted, swap, LVM, RAID, multipath and unknown devices before detach
Flush and quiesce I/O and verify no open handles under the approved storage procedure
Do not equate disappearance from `nvme list` with safe removal without the vendor oracle
Preserve logs and do not physically pull the drive unless separately approved
Abort on active use, wrong identity, I/O/media error, device reset/loss outside plan, LED mismatch or physical fault; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate storage identity, active-stack exclusions, approved readiness transition and recovery
Collect read-only inventory/health/state evidence and organize operator photos
Perform a state-changing offline/detach only after exact command and separate execution approval
Do not select a target, infer LED/state, physically remove hardware, clear logs, retry detach or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve bay/drive/namespace map and exact ready-to-remove transition/oracle
Approve LED combination, all-bay population, physical-removal scope and final state
Review state/visual/health evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsblk` and `nvme list` identify drives but neither quiesces them nor proves the safe-removal state or physical LED combination. Its SSH method is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the vendor-approved offline/detach or enclosure readiness procedure against the proven drive identity after quiescence; operator records the exact LED state, and no physical removal occurs without separate approval.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The insertion, ready-to-remove condition, solid-white/amber-off/green-off criterion and 10/10-minute estimate remain; trigger and safe-removal semantics are pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate an approved logical safe-removal transition and active-stack proof with timestamped direct observation of the exact three-channel bay indicator.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a defined readiness trigger, data-safety checks, simultaneous LED oracle, no-pull boundary and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Enumeration, device disappearance or any single LED color alone cannot prove the complete safe-removal state.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Offlining the wrong namespace can interrupt or corrupt services; different platforms assert removal LEDs through OS, enclosure or BMC controls, so the action cannot be guessed.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must distinguish `ready to remove` from merely powered, logically offline, surprise-removed and physically absent. `All E1.s` requires a population matrix and per-bay supported removal method.
expected_evidence: Backplane/bay/controller/drive/namespace identity and approved service procedure
Exact readiness command/action, output, timestamp and post-transition logical state
Per-bay photo/video showing solid white with amber and green simultaneously off
Preserved NVMe/dmesg/journal/BMC/SEL/AER, no-pull/final-state/recovery record and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently defines the ready-to-remove LED combination. DeepSeek's enumeration-only approach is incomplete, but the source identity and visual criterion are not contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The safe-removal/LED objective is clear. Platform trigger, storage map, quiesce and LED specification are supplyable prerequisites, so execution is approval-gated rather than blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2216 Wistron-HW-00491-V002: approve the chassis/backplane and complete bay/slot/controller-to-drive serial/model/firmware/namespace matrix, meaning of 'All E1.s', exact vendor ready-to-remove trigger/state and command path, mount/open-handle/multipath/RAID/LVM quiesce plus backup rules, solid-white with amber/green-off timing oracle, whether physical removal is excluded or required, hot-plug/ESD procedure, aborts, final state and recovery.

review_improvement: Restores the missing safe-removal transition and physical three-color LED coverage while preventing wrong-target detach, data loss, unsafe pulling and software-only inference.
independent_technical_reasoning: Ready-to-remove is a controlled state transition, not an attribute visible from ordinary enumeration. A drive can still appear in `nvme list` after being quiesced, or disappear because of a fault rather than safe removal, so the authoritative platform control and active-stack proof are essential. The three LED channels must be observed simultaneously because white on with amber or green still active fails the stated criterion. Physical removal expands risk and is not authorized by the wording that only asks to observe the ready state.
